newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad Rotterdam 9-mth net seen up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stad Rotterdam 9-mth net seen up 13 pct.

text.p: Mid-sized Dutch insurer Stad Rotterdam Anno 1720 NV is expected to announce a 13 percent rise in nine-month net profits on Thursday, November 14, analysts said.
Thirteen analysts polled by Reuters forecast Stad Rotterdam's profits to range between 99 and 102 million guilders, with a consensus at 101.3 million guilders.
In the same 1995 period profits were 89.3 million guilders.
Analysts expect a strong increase in pre-tax profits in the non-life sector, with motor insurance back in the black after posting a loss in 1995.
Analysts said motor insurance made a pre-tax loss of 15 million guilders for the whole of 1995 and they forecast full-year pre-tax 1996 profits of around 10 million guilders.
"The strength for the moment could be the weakness of the future, though," said Van Lanschot analyst Jean-Paul van Bavel.
"Non-life remains cyclical and the danger exists that profits could start fading again in this sector," he said.

In a research note, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said Stad Rotterdam would post a 13 percent increase in net profit over the first nine months compared to an expected 16 percent rise at bigger rival Aegon, 24 percent for Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING) and 15 percent at Fortis Amev.
"We expect life results to show a lower growth rate than last year, as a result of higher provisions and marketing costs," the note said.
Stad Rotterdam's life premium income rose a moderate seven percent to 648 million guilders in the first half of 1996.
Analysts said Stad Rotterdam might do better to focus more on life insurances instead of non-life as earnings growth was more stable in this field.
Analyst Bart van der Feen-Delille at IRIS Securities said Stad Rotterdam could score with products it developed as a result of the abolition of the Dutch Sickness and Benefit Act.
"This year I do not foresee profits in this sector, but in the longer run there are good opportunities," he said.
